tldr: NVIDIA's open Nemotron family widened on Oct 28 with Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2 for promptable multilingual transcription. A day later AWS published a guide to running the 120B-parameter Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS.
whats_new: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter multimodal model, is now a managed option in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, deployable as an NVFP4 or BF16 variant.
why_it_matters: Nemotron 3.5 now has two AWS deployment paths, self-managed Kubernetes (EKS, HyperPod EKS) and managed JumpStart, plus a speech model, so an open-weight stack can be trialed without building serving infrastructure first.

status.detail: Nemotron 3.5 has moved from model releases to packaged deployment on AWS, with Super VL now in JumpStart.

beats.headline: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2 target promptable multilingual transcription
beats.summary: NVIDIA extends the family into speech with a model that can be prompted and adapted.

beats.headline: AWS shows Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS
beats.summary: A 120B mixture-of-experts model combining reasoning, tool use and multimodal understanding gets a Kubernetes deployment walkthrough.

beats.headline: Super VL lands in SageMaker JumpStart in NVFP4 and BF16 variants
beats.summary: A managed deploy path now covers text, image and video inference.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm Nemotron 3.5 Super VL's reasoning and tool-use quality against closed multimodal models?
How do NVFP4 and BF16 JumpStart deployments compare on latency, cost and accuracy for the same workload?
Will Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe appear as a managed option on AWS or other clouds?
take_for_builders: If you run multimodal agents on AWS, deploy both the NVFP4 and BF16 Super VL variants from JumpStart against your own eval set and compare cost and accuracy before choosing one.
